kind: Android device verification on an emulator (not a physical phone)

build.install: adb install -r (Success, in-place upgrade over the previous install)
build.instrumentedNotificationProvider: tools/notifier-fixture (applicationId com.whatsapp, posts Notification.MessagingStyle with category msg)

checks.check: install, first launch, disclosure, hub render
checks.detail: Disclosure accepted; hub rendered 'bop', 'Alerts on', '2 spaces / 1 apps'.

checks.check: notification ingestion from an observed package (matrix row 1 on hardware)
commands: adb shell am broadcast -a com.whatsapp.FIXTURE_POST -p com.whatsapp
checks.detail: Hub posted NotificationRecord pkg=com.example.twoaccmess tag=hub-account-C id=102 with InboxStyle, title 'Account C has messages in 2 chats' and lines 'Sam: hello C', 'Sam: hello one'. Slot C was bound to WhatsApp through the picker; the fixture notification carried no account id of its own.
Hub card for C removed; source notifications untouched.

checks.check: listener revocation and re-grant does not resurrect a dismissed card (D5 on hardware)
checks.detail: After reconnect the dismissed card did not return (0 hub cards). A new fixture message afterwards posted exactly one new card, so ingestion still worked after the reconnect.

checks.check: POST_NOTIFICATIONS revoked: alert recorded, no card (matrix row 15 on hardware)
commands: adb shell pm revoke com.example.twoaccmess android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS
checks.detail: 0 hub cards while the permission was denied.

checks.check: POST_NOTIFICATIONS re-granted: pending alert becomes visible again
commands: adb shell pm grant com.example.twoaccmess android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS
checks.result: failed before this change, passed after
checks.detail: Before: 0 cards after returning to the hub, and none appeared until a later message arrived. After HubNotifications.restore on resume: the card is re-posted silently (1 card) and the already-delivered alert is visible outside the app again.

checks.check: Doze / forced deep idle (matrix row 11 on hardware)
checks.detail: dumpsys deviceidle reported IDLE; the next message still produced a hub card (1).

Hub relaunched with the same 3 spaces / 2 apps and 'Alerts on'; no Java crash in the crash buffer. One native SIGILL was recorded in :messenger_c inside libwebviewchromium (WebViewChromium.onTrimMemory) while that background slot was being reclaimed; see limitations.

checks.check: reboot with multiple spaces (matrix row 12 on hardware)
checks.detail: After boot: 3 spaces / 2 apps, notification access still granted, hub installed without waiting for a tap, no crash.

commands: adb shell run-as com.example.twoaccmess cat files/space-index.json
adb shell run-as com.example.twoaccmess ls shared_prefs
checks.detail: space-index.json = [{A,messenger},{B,messenger},{C,whatsapp}]; shared_prefs contains web-space-C.xml, i.e. each slot keeps its own preferences file.

limitations: An emulator is not a physical phone: OEM battery managers, real Doze calibration, real WebView builds and real provider notifications are not exercised.
The fixture posts under com.whatsapp with a synthetic MessagingStyle notification; it proves the listener, filter, attribution, card and permission paths, not WhatsApp's own notification format.
No web slot was signed in, so the web-title path (WebUnread -> WebAlertReceiver) was covered by JVM tests only.

One native SIGILL (signal 4, libwebviewchromium WebViewChromium.onTrimMemory) occurred in :messenger_c while the background slot's process was being reclaimed after an am kill. It did not reproduce on a plain launch, and no app frame appears in the tombstone; it is recorded here rather than claimed fixed.
